# Hermes Agent FAQ & Onboarding Guide

### 1. Installation & Platforms
- **Native Windows**: Tier 1 supported via PowerShell (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is only needed for the Web Dashboard embedded terminal (`/chat`), which requires a POSIX PTY.
- **Docker & NAS**: Multi-arch image (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) supports `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Raspberry Pi / Apple Silicon). For NAS bind-mount permission issues (UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID), pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) to match host file ownership.
- **Android / Termux**: Supported via `install.sh`; sets temp files to `$TMPDIR`, supplies `ANDROID_API_LEVEL`, and installs the curated `[termux-all]` dependency group.
- **Web Interface**: Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local UI and browser chat at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`.
- **Update Behavior**: Slow Node.js steps during `hermes update` are caused by Camofox postinstall silently downloading browser binaries.

### 2. Model Providers & Configuration
- **Small Local Models (Ollama / Qwen 4B–9B)**: Slow responses occur because Hermes sends ~45 tool schemas per turn. Mitigate by disabling unused tools via `hermes tools`, using faster quantizations, switching to 32B+ models, or setting `terminal.backend: local`.
- **Local Endpoint Overrides**: When `provider: auto` detects remote environment keys (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), it bypasses local endpoints. Explicitly set `provider: custom` and `base_url: http://localhost:11434` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- **Custom Vision & Token Usage**: Set `supports_vision: true` for custom vision models. For local OpenAI-compatible servers (LocalAI), Hermes sends `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` on streams and forwards `extra_body` settings.
- **Ollama Cloud**: Fixed in v0.15.0+ (v2026.5.28); uses `provider: ollama-cloud` which correctly routes to the OpenAI-compatible `https://ollama.com/v1` endpoint instead of `/api`.
- **Azure Foundry & Gemini**: For Azure AI Foundry, set `provider: azure-foundry` with `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`. Legacy Gemini CLI OAuth is removed; use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs API**: API keys are always billed per token by Anthropic. To use Pro/Max subscription quotas, authenticate via OAuth.
- **DeepSeek V4 Pricing Discrepancy**: Model normalization previously rewrote `deepseek-v4-flash` to `deepseek-chat` (mapped by DeepSeek to the pricier `deepseek-v4-pro`). Update or configure canonical model names.
- **Model Routing**: Automatic complexity routing (`smart_model_routing`) is deliberately not supported. Switch models manually (`/model`, `hermes chat -m <model>`) or set `delegation.model` for subagents.

### 3. Messaging Gateways & Personas
- **Gateway Setup**: Run `hermes gateway setup` for an interactive wizard to configure platform tokens (Discord, Telegram, etc.) without manual `.env` editing.
- **Telegram Authorization**: `allowed_chats` is only a group filter. To authorize private DMs, add your numeric user ID to `telegram.allow_from` in `config.yaml`, or run `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
- **Session Restarts & Telegram Resets**: Handled via `resume_pending`, preserving session IDs and transcripts across restarts. Idle resets default to `mode: none` (opt-in).
- **Files & Media**: Inbound attachments (`.txt`, `.py`) are automatically ingested. Outbound delivery is natively supported for Matrix (`m.file`), email (SMTP multipart), DingTalk (Markdown `![image](url)`), and Telegram. Standard MCP `ImageContent` results are cached and surfaced natively via `MEDIA:<path>`.
- **Open WebUI Streaming**: Missing tool progress was fixed in v2026.4.8 by correcting the 4-argument `tool_progress_callback` signature in `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`.
- **Profiles & Multiplexing**: Multiple accounts/channels (including WeChat/Weixin and Telegram) can run under multiplexed gateway profiles, keeping sessions, memory, and credentials fully isolated. Configure channel-specific prompts via `channel_prompts`, and subagents via `delegate_task`.

### 4. Memory, Tools & Context
- **Memory Files & User Scaffolds**: `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` stores agent persona; `USER.md` stores user profile/preferences (`target="user"`); `MEMORY.md` stores long-term facts. Fixed in v2026.7.1 so installers seed complete scaffolds.
- **Honcho Localhost**: Fixed in v2026.3.30+ to accept either `api_key` or `base_url`, injecting `"local"` as a placeholder key for `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` instances.
- **Custom Plugins & Tools**: In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Implement external plugins subclassing `MemoryProvider` or register custom tools via `ctx.register_tool(...)` inside `~/.hermes/plugins/`, then enable with `hermes plugins enable <name>`.
- **Context Management**: Tool output bloat is mitigated built-in via `ContextCompressor` (prunes/deduplicates old tool results before compaction) and the pluggable `ContextEngine` interface (`context.engine`).
- **Autonomy & Limits**: Default turn limit is `agent.max_turns: 90` (override via `--max-turns <N>`). Long multi-turn tasks use `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop), which persists across turns and resumes with `/goal resume`.

### 5. Observability & Security
- **Diagnostics & Tracing**: Run `hermes doctor` to validate environment and auth. Track call chains with Langfuse via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Skill Telemetry**: Track execution counts and history via `/insights` or `hermes insights` (stored in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).
- **Vulnerability Reporting**: Report security issues privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com`.
